title: Is Your Plan Really Working? | Principles of Management Ep 19
description:
The bus stand Chai Corner has been open for a month. The plan was 500 cups a day, but some cups are half empty, some customers wait five minutes, and nobody has counted a single cup. In this animated lesson, Ravi and Kabir learn controlling: checking the real work against the plan, and fixing the gap.

You will see Kabir at the cash box and ledger, then watch the control loop run step by step: set the standard, measure the real work, compare, find the cause, and correct it, while a live chart shows sales climbing from 400 back to the 500 target. We look at why planning and controlling are called the twins of management, at control before, during and after the work (feedforward, concurrent and feedback control), and at F.W. Taylor's exception principle from Shop Management, 1903. Then controlling at work today: delivery promises, factory defect counts, budget against actual spending, pilots' pre-flight checklists, and banks flagging unusual payments. Finally the human side: too much checking hurts trust, and people can chase the number instead of the goal, which economist Charles Goodhart warned about in 1975.

This is Episode 19 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
